solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Translucent boil mostly having an uneven surface (3-7)

indicators.note: 'mostly' means most of it but not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: seethe = boil, minus its last E
the rough, as on a golf course, is uneven ground

annotation.surface: A description of a nasty skin blister, pale and bumpy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a medical note about a boil; 'boil' is really the verb, as in water seething.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fabric that lets light through, so you can almost see through it, is translucent.

entries.clue: Bargain hunter finding fish higher in price! (7,2)

annotation.surface: A shopper at the fishmonger's discovers the fish has gone up in price.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Shakespeare's Autolycus, 'a snapper-up of unconsidered trifles'; the exclamation mark flags the shopper's dismay.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary idiom: someone who grabs goods the moment they appear cheap is exactly what a bargain hunter is.

entries.clue: Old academic flipped over introduction of standardised tests (5)

indicators.note: something flipped over lies the other way up, so in a down entry its letters run in reverse
the introduction is the opening of a thing, so take the word's first letter

blocks.note: MA, a Master of Arts, turned round

annotation.surface: An elderly professor loses his temper at the arrival of standardised testing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipped' sounds like losing one's temper; it only turns MA round. EX is the usual crossword prefix for 'old'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: school and university tests, especially formal written ones, are called exams.

entries.clue: Pity each revolutionary’s grief (9)

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters of EACH do not stay in theirs

blocks.note: heart = compassion, as in 'have a heart'

annotation.surface: A lament for the sorrow each revolutionary carries.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as a noun, a rebel; it is an adjective telling you to rearrange EACH. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the emotional pain of loss or disappointment, felt as if in the chest, is grief.

entries.clue: Experiencing a spell of good luck when student managed to block toilet up (2,1,4)

definitions.text: Experiencing a spell of good luck

indicators.note: a blockage sits inside a pipe, so RAN goes inside the toilet
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run in reverse

annotation.surface: A lucky streak for a student who manages to block the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: Assemble L + LO(RAN)O = LLORANO, then read it upwards. 'Block toilet up' pretends to be a plumbing mishap, and a toilet roll lurks in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a gambler on a roll keeps winning, so it means enjoying a run of good luck.

entries.clue: German porkies describing soldiers’ triumphs (7)

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so LIES goes around OR

blocks.note: porkies = pork pies, rhyming slang for lies

annotation.surface: German propaganda exaggerating the army's victories.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Porkies' is British slang for lies, from the rhyming slang pork pies. 'Describing' looks like narrating the soldiers' deeds; it means drawing round them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: past triumphs are the glories of a career or an army.

entries.clue: Greek god’s accuser apparently hiding on the way back (4)

indicators.note: something hiding is tucked inside other words, here inside 'accuser apparently'
going back means travelling the other way, so read the letters from right to left

blocks.note: accuSER Apparently, read right to left

annotation.surface: A god's accuser seems to be lying low as he returns home.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so 'Greek god' is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the Greek god of war, whom the Romans called Mars.

entries.clue: Relating to a religious movement of friars at a bash (9)

indicators.note: to bash something is to knock it out of shape, so the letters before it are knocked about

annotation.surface: Friars letting their hair down at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bash' reads as a party, the friars' night out; it is the instruction to knock the letters about.
annotation.definitionFit: The name of the Jamaican religious movement is also used as its adjective, as in 'Rastafari beliefs'.

entries.clue: Maiden cutting a little flower (5)

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another sits within it, so M goes inside the other word

blocks.note: M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

annotation.surface: A young woman snipping a small bloom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river, something that flows. M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a flower is anything that flows, and the Somme flows through northern France.

entries.clue: A literary sub-genre, on the other hand, not concerned with pursuing fun (3,4)

indicators.note: being 'in' something means being concerned with it, so remove the letters IN
a pursuer comes behind what it chases, so this piece follows the other

blocks.clueFragment: on the other hand, not concerned with
blocks.note: again = on the other hand, minus IN

annotation.surface: A critic dismisses a kind of fiction as not about having fun.
annotation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' does double duty, in the definition and the wordplay. An Aga is a British cast-iron cooking range, the emblem of the comfortable country kitchen.
annotation.definitionFit: A named genre: Aga sagas are novels about middle-class English country life, named after the kitchen range.

entries.clue: Marsupial mouse endlessly swimming across river heading south (7)

indicators.note: without an end, so the word loses its last letter
things swimming move about freely, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters stretch across the next pieces, enclosing them
a heading is a compass direction, here south

annotation.surface: A small marsupial swims across a river heading south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marsupial mouse' reads as one creature, but the definition is 'Marsupial' alone; the mouse is raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the opossum of the Americas carries its young in a pouch, so it is a marsupial.

entries.clue: Evident in Robin’s charm (3)

indicators.note: what is evident in something can be seen within it, so look inside the next word

annotation.surface: Robin's charm is plain to see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charm' suggests charisma; it is the object, a magic token.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in the Caribbean, obi (or obeah) is folk sorcery, and also a charm or fetish used in it.

entries.clue: Put forward as fact in online comment embracing individualism at the outset (5)

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so the comment holds the letter inside
the outset is the very start, so take the first letter

annotation.surface: Someone online asserting the virtues of individualism.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Online comment' is a noun here, a forum post, though the surface lets it read as the setting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in philosophy: to assume something as a basis for argument is to put it forward as fact.

entries.clue: Start to hold forth about Gail oddly back at home (9)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the speech goes around the rest
take the odd-numbered letters, first and third
going back means reversing, so those letters run the other way

blocks.note: orate = hold forth, make a speech
GaIl's odd letters G, I, reversed

annotation.surface: Gail, strangely, has started lecturing everyone back at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a comment on Gail's behaviour; it picks her odd letters. 'Back at home' reads as a phrase but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to originate is to begin or come into being, which is to start.

entries.clue: Unnamed cardinal surprisingly thorough (7)

indicators.note: unnamed means without a name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so remove N
something turning out surprisingly is not in the expected order, so rearrange

annotation.surface: An anonymous cardinal proves unexpectedly thorough.
annotation.walkthrough: An 'unnamed cardinal' sounds like an anonymous Vatican source; it is CARDINAL with N removed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: radical comes from Latin radix, root, so a radical change goes to the root and is thorough.

entries.clue: Become extremely agitated and tense after literary Lorna’s letter (2,4,3)

indicators.note: a thing placed after another comes later, so T goes at the end

blocks.note: Lorna Doone, heroine of Blackmore's novel

annotation.surface: Lorna Doone's letter makes someone agitated and tense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence; it is the Greek letter. 'Tense' looks like a mood; it is the grammatical abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional idiom: British slang for flying into a rage, the nut being one's head.

entries.clue: Shame about American bear (7)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the shame goes around the American

annotation.surface: Embarrassment about an American bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' pretends to be the animal, fitting 'American'; it is the verb, to carry or endure.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sustain weight or losses is to bear them.

entries.clue: That baked dish included in South Carolina exhibition primarily as a fine example of its type (9)

indicators.note: things included in a group sit within it, so these letters go inside the state
primarily means first of all, so take the first letter

blocks.note: that = how, as in 'she told me that/how he left'
a pie is a baked dish

annotation.surface: A pie on show at a South Carolina fair, held up as the best of its kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That' can stand in for 'how' in reported speech; it is the hardest piece to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a showpiece is the item put on display because it is outstanding, a fine example of its type.

entries.clue: Information turned over by the French court newspaper boss disregarded (9)

indicators.note: something turned over is upside down, so in a down entry its letters read in reverse

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor ignores information handed over by a French court.
annotation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something neglected has been ignored or not attended to, that is, disregarded.

entries.clue: Went without my turn to advance (7)

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps around the second
to turn is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: cor! = my!, both exclamations of surprise, reversed

annotation.surface: Someone missed their turn before moving on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking; here it means outside. 'Went' is a coy euphemism, and 'cor' is a British exclamation like 'my!'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go forward or carry on is to advance.

entries.clue: Think at length of Spanish gentleman keeping in good health (5,2)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the gentleman holds the health word inside him

blocks.note: Don, Spanish title for a gentleman

annotation.surface: Musing about a Spanish gentleman staying healthy.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition needs its preposition from the answer: 'think at length (of)' pairs with the phrasal verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to linger over a subject in thought or speech is to think at length about it.

entries.clue: Wise monarch accepting immediately (7)

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the monarch takes the other word inside

annotation.surface: A wise king agrees at once.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Accepting immediately' reads as a prompt yes; it is a container with its contents.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a knowing look shows shrewd understanding, which is being wise.

entries.clue: Of fundamental importance to mention diagram of identification at the front (7)

indicators.note: something at the front comes first, so this piece leads even though it comes second in the clue

blocks.note: a map's key identifies its symbols

annotation.surface: A caption that points to the legend of a map.
annotation.walkthrough: Used as an adjective, as in 'keynote speech'; in music the keynote is the note a key is built on, hence fundamental.
annotation.definitionFit: An attributive use: a keynote address sets out the central theme, so it is of fundamental importance.

entries.clue: Betrayal of Republican entrapped by schoolmaster at end of story (9)

indicators.note: something entrapped is caught inside, so R goes inside the schoolmaster
take the letter at the end of the word

annotation.surface: A Republican tricked by a teacher in a tale of betrayal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of story' reads as a flat full stop to an argument; it gives only the Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: treachery is the betrayal of trust.

entries.clue: Understood by Italian leader engaged in diplomacy (5)

indicators.note: the leader goes first, so take the first letter
someone engaged in an activity is inside it, so the letter goes within diplomacy

annotation.surface: An Italian politician's grasp of diplomacy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian leader' suggests a prime minister; it is only the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tacit agreement is understood without being spoken aloud.

entries.clue: Copper meeting resistance from scoundrel (3)

indicators.note: two things meeting come together side by side, so the pieces join end to end

blocks.note: Cu, the chemical symbol for copper
R, the symbol for electrical resistance

annotation.surface: A policeman encounters resistance from a villain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer, which fits the scene; here it is the metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cur is a mongrel dog, and by extension a contemptible man, a scoundrel.

entries.clue: Put in position by expert on Poland (5)

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another sits after it, so the expert follows the country

annotation.surface: Someone installed in a post by a Polish specialist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expert on Poland' reads as a specialist in Polish affairs; 'on' is only ordering the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set something in a spot is to put it in position.

entries.clue: Modify American person’s home over time (5)

indicators.note: something turned over faces the other way, so the home word runs backwards

blocks.note: one's pad is one's home, reversed

annotation.surface: Remodelling an American's house over time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pad' is slang for a flat or home. 'Over time' reads as a phrase meaning gradually, but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to change something to suit new conditions is to modify it.

entries.clue: Lacking enthusiasm to take in books on royal authority (7)

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the cool word surrounds the rest
in an across entry, books on royal means books placed before R, sitting on it

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A half-hearted reader of books about royal power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books on royal authority' reads as a reading list; the definition is only 'authority'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having control over people means having authority over them.

entries.clue: Shown openly eating Bill’s ham (7)

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater, so the open word takes the bill inside it

annotation.surface: Bill is seen publicly tucking into his ham.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name and 'ham' like his lunch; the 's is 'is', and 'ham' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre verb: to ham is to perform with exaggerated gestures, as a bad actor does.

entries.clue: Carry young child easily at first (4)

indicators.note: 'at first' means at the very beginning, so take the word's opening letter

blocks.note: a tot is a small child

annotation.surface: Carrying a toddler with no trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads straight as picking up a toddler, and TOT is right there inside the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly American: to tote a bag or a gun is to carry it around.

entries.clue: Entire set split up before daughter becomes personally involved (10)

indicators.note: a set that is split up is broken into pieces and scattered, so rearrange its letters
something before another comes ahead of it, so the daughter goes last

annotation.surface: A family breaks up and the daughter gets personally caught up in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Split up' suggests a separation; it is the instruction to rearrange. 'Becomes' links, reading as 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: an interested party has a personal stake in the outcome, not just curiosity.
